## My request:
Now please start the investigation trying to lower \delta, with the goal of obtaining an initial promising result for the research program

I’ll investigate a first fixed power saving, starting from the signed covariance formulation. I’ll look for a concrete arithmetic mechanism, test its exponent budget, and record either a promising lemma or a precise obstruction rather than treating finite-range improvements as a global reduction.

An exact Möbius divisor identity looks useful: the probe’s zero mean suppresses the contribution from a large range of divisors, leaving a much shorter sum over small cofactors. I’m checking the cutoff needed to put the discarded part on the quadratic scale, then testing the surviving signed sum numerically. This would give a concrete arithmetic target, though not yet a smaller global \(\delta\).

The reduction is now proved: divisors through \(X^{11/12}/(\log X)^{1/6}\) contribute only \(O(X^2)\) variance. The remaining sum has cofactors of size \(O(X^{1/12}(\log X)^{1/6})\). A bounded pilot shows substantial cancellation between those cofactor terms, but it supplies no global exponent bound. I’m now checking the proof independently and assessing which known arithmetic estimates could apply.

The proof and independent code checks pass. A slightly wider retained range gives a stronger remainder bound: keeping cofactors up to \(O(X^{1/10})\) leaves discarded energy \(O(X^{9/5}\log^2 X)\), below the quadratic scale. I’ve recorded this result, the supporting reductions, the pilot, and the precise estimate still needed to lower the global exponent.
